reason: This passage from 2 Samuel 13 describes internal conflict within the royal family regarding Amnon's assault on his sister Tamar. The antagonism portrayed is between family members (Amnon, Tamar, Absalom, and King David), not between regular people and their leader. While David becomes angry when he learns of the crime, this represents a father/king's response to a crime committed by his own son, not antagonism from the general population toward their ruler. All the characters involved in the conflict are members of the royal household or court.
